Here's the secret to every circle question on the SAT. Find one number, the radius, and the circle tells you everything else.
Picture a dog tied to a stake with a leash. The leash is pulled tight, and the dog runs as far as it can, all the way around.
The path it runs is a circle. The stake is the center. The leash is the radius, r. Every point on the circle is exactly one leash length from the center.
Now tie a second dog on the other side. Leash plus leash, straight through the center, is the diameter. So the diameter is two r.
How far does the dog run in one lap? That distance around is the circumference, C.
Cut the circle open and roll it out into a straight rope.
Now lay the diameter along that rope. It fits three times, plus a little bit more. That number, about three point one four, is pi.
So the distance around is pi times the diameter. C equals pi d, which is the same as two pi r.
Now the area: how much pizza is inside. Cut the pizza into skinny slices.
Flip every other slice and line them up. They make a shape that is almost a rectangle.
The height is the radius, r. The bottom is half the crust. Half of two pi r is pi r.
A rectangle's area is base times height. Pi r times r. That's pi r squared.
Here's the twist the SAT loves. Double the radius, and the area does not double. It gets four times bigger.
That's because r gets squared. Two squared is four. Triple the radius, and three squared gives nine times the area.
Last piece. An arc is part of the crust. A sector is one slice of the pizza. Both are just a fraction of the whole circle.
The fraction is the angle over three sixty, because one full turn is three hundred sixty degrees.
Let's try an SAT style question. A circle has a radius of six. A central angle measures sixty degrees. What is the arc length?
Step one, the fraction. Sixty over three sixty is one sixth.
Step two, the whole crust. C equals two pi r. Two times pi times six is twelve pi.
Step three, take one sixth of twelve pi. The arc length is two pi.
Trap alert. Don't use pi r squared here. Arc length is part of the crust, so it comes from the circumference, not the area.
Your turn. Pause the video. A circle has a radius of five. What is its area?
Area is pi r squared. Five squared is twenty five, so the area is twenty five pi. If you got ten pi, you found the circumference by mistake.
Remember three things. Find r first. Distance around is two pi r. Space inside is pi r squared. Great work.
